fields.sample_size: six purposively selected cities in Africa, Asia and South America (including Ahmedabad, Phnom Penh, Abidjan and Porto Alegre) chosen from country clusters; case-specific literature plus 1-3 key-informant interviews per case; modified social-ecological systems framework
fields.effect_estimate: Three types of progress were observed -- utility-driven, regulator-supported and municipality-driven -- and 12 characteristics of the enabling environment were identified across them under two themes: a well-functioning water service provider (clear performance indicators, customer feedback, sustainable operating-cost financing) is often a prerequisite for inclusive service, and inclusive services often need explicit pro-poor policies and strategies. Selection was of 'successful' cities, so the findings describe correlates of success in selected cases, not tested causal effects. Funded by USAID, which gave input on research questions.
fields.study_design: qualitative comparative case study (six cities; literature review plus key-informant interviews; modified SES framework)
fields.section: Full text: Methods (case selection from clusters, framework, data); Results (six cases, three types of progress); Discussion 4.2 (12 characteristics)
fields.exact_location: Methods (case selection from clusters, framework, data); Results (six cases, three types of progress); Discussion 4.2 (12 characteristics)

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a comparative case study of six 'successful' cities (e.g. Ahmedabad, Phnom Penh, Abidjan, Porto Alegre) in inclusive piped water provision, read in full text 2026-10-04. Utility-driven, regulator-supported and municipality-driven paths; 12 enabling characteristics including performance indicators and explicit pro-poor policies. Selected-success design.
pdf_note: PLOS Water (2023), about 143,000 characters read; supplementary text not read
notes: Abstract-level extraction accurate; names example cities and the selection design (success-selected cases). Funder gave input on research questions.
